fault_line: Truce in Kherson, slaughter at the station: is the Oleshky ceasefire a real diplomatic opening or cover while civilian rail targets keep burning?

sections.what_happened: [ATTRIBUTED REPORT - UPDATE, NO NEW STRIKE] Reuters reports the Dnipro railway-station drone strike killed AT LEAST 14 people, matching Kyiv Independent's 14 and resolving the 1900-10 toll conflict as time-progression: Zelenskyy's midday '13 confirmed as of now' was an earlier snapshot, the toll rose to at least 14 later in the day. Reuters adds 5 more killed elsewhere Thursday: 2 teenagers on a central street in Chernihiv (23 wounded) and 3 in a strike on an apartment building in Kremenchuk. The six-day Oleshky humanitarian truce is holding into its third day, with Ukraine's human-rights ombudsman Dmytro Lubinets announcing he had set out with the Ukrainian delegation toward Oleshky via Belarus and Russia. CNA/AFP still carries the stale midday 13 figure.
sections.what_verified: Two declared-tier families agree on 14 for Dnipro (Reuters T1, Kyiv Independent T2); CNA (T2) carries the older 13 figure, consistent with an earlier snapshot rather than a contradiction. Truce-holding and delegation movement corroborated by Reuters reporting of Lubinets' announcement.
sections.what_disputed: Moscow denies deliberately targeting civilians (standing denial, via Reuters). CNA/AFP's 13 figure shows the toll was still being reported as 13 in some wires late in the day; casualty counts remain fluid and no single consolidated official release reconciles killed vs wounded across outlets.
sections.why_matters: The toll moved while the wires slept: 13 at noon, 14 by evening — and the truce held anyway. Dnipro's number is now settled enough to run, with the truce as the twist.
